buildServers.title: Build servers
buildServers.description: Register build servers globally, define triggerable workflows, and assign them to projects. Projects only see their assigned workflows — never the server or its credentials.
buildServers.name: Name

baseUrlHint.GITLAB_CI: Instance root, e.g. https://gitlab.com. Must use https; private addresses are rejected.
baseUrlHint.GITHUB_ACTIONS: API root: https://api.github.com, or https://ghe.example.com/api/v3 for Enterprise Server.

tokenHint.GITLAB_CI: Personal or project access token with api scope. Stored encrypted, never returned.
tokenHint.GITHUB_ACTIONS: Fine-grained token with Actions read/write on the repositories. Stored encrypted, never returned.
tokenHint.FORGEJO_ACTIONS: Access token with repository scope. Stored encrypted, never returned.
tokenHint.WOODPECKER: Personal token from your Woodpecker user settings. Stored encrypted, never returned.
tokenHint.JENKINS: Enter as user:apiToken. Stored encrypted, never returned.
tokenHint.AZURE_DEVOPS: Personal access token. Stored encrypted, never returned.

buildServers.deleteMessage: "{{name}}" and all its workflow definitions will be removed. Past pipeline runs keep their history.
buildServers.noWorkflows: No workflows defined on this server yet.
buildServers.discoveryUnsupported: This provider has no list to discover from — enter the workflow manually.
buildServers.workflowNameHint: Shown to testers, e.g. "Nightly regression suite".
buildServers.workflowRefHint: For GitHub/Forgejo Actions: the workflow file name, e.g. tests.yml. Leave empty for GitLab, Woodpecker and Jenkins.
buildServers.defaultParametersHint: One KEY=value per line. Testers can override them per run.
buildServers.assignedProjectsHint: Only assigned projects can see and trigger this workflow.
buildServers.deleteWorkflowMessage: "{{name}}" will be removed from all projects. Past pipeline runs keep their history.

issueTracker.title: Issue tracker
issueTracker.description: Connect this project to an issue tracker so testers can link or file defects from a failed result.
issueTracker.providerHint: Only trackers with an available adapter are listed.
issueTracker.baseUrlHint: Must use https. Private and loopback addresses are rejected.
issueTracker.tokenHint: Stored encrypted. Requires ISSUE_TRACKER_ENCRYPTION_KEY to be configured on the server.
issueTracker.tokenStoredHint: A token is stored. Leave empty to keep it.
issueTracker.accountEmailHint: The Atlassian account the API token belongs to. Jira Cloud signs in with the two together.

tokenHelp.GITLAB: GitLab: a project or personal access token with the "api" scope.
tokenHelp.FORGEJO: Forgejo / Gitea: an access token with read and write permission on issues.
tokenHelp.GITHUB: GitHub: a fine-grained personal access token with "Issues: Read and write" on this repository, or a classic token with the "repo" scope.
tokenHelp.JIRA: Jira Cloud: an API token from id.atlassian.com, plus the account email. Jira Data Center: a personal access token from your profile. If the project requires extra fields when creating an issue, file it in Jira and link it here.

issueTracker.activeHint: When inactive, no calls are made to the tracker and linking is unavailable.
issueTracker.deleteMessage: This project will no longer be able to search, link or create issues.
issueTracker.deleteKeepsLinks: Issues already linked to results are kept and stay clickable.
issueTracker.noLinkedIssues: No issues linked to this result.
issueTracker.searchHint: Type to search the connected tracker.
issueTracker.searchFailed: Could not search the tracker. It may be unreachable or the token may be invalid.

sso.title: Single sign-on
sso.description: Let people sign in with your identity provider. Any OpenID Connect provider works — Keycloak, Authentik, Auth0, Okta, Entra ID, Google.
sso.slugHint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. Used in the callback URL.
sso.slugLockedHint: The slug cannot change — your provider already knows the callback URL.
sso.callbackUrlHint: Register this exact URL with your identity provider.
sso.protocolHint: OpenID Connect covers almost everything. GitHub is the exception — it publishes no discovery document.
sso.protocolLockedHint: The protocol cannot change — the accounts already linked to this provider depend on it.
sso.issuerUriHint: The discovery root. Must use https; private and loopback addresses are rejected.
sso.gitHubUrlHint: https://github.com, or your GitHub Enterprise Server address.
sso.gitHubMappingNote: GitHub returns no claims, so email and name are read from its API and system administrator has to be granted on the user. Your OAuth app's callback URL must match the one above exactly.
sso.clientSecretHint: Stored encrypted. Requires APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY on the server.
sso.clientSecretStoredHint: A secret is stored. Leave empty to keep it.
sso.adminClaimHint: Optional. Grants system admin when this claim holds the value below.
sso.autoProvisionHint: New people get an account with no project access until you add them to a project.
sso.trustEmail: Trust this provider's email for account linking
sso.trustEmailHint: Only enable for a provider that controls which email addresses its users can claim. When enabled, someone signing in with a verified email that matches an existing account takes over that account.
sso.activeHint: Inactive providers are hidden from the sign-in screen and reject new logins.
sso.deleteMessage: {{name}} will be removed and its sign-in button will disappear.
sso.deleteLosesAccess: Anyone who can only sign in through it will lose access.
sso.localLoginHint: When off, only single sign-on is available. System admins can always sign in with a password, so a broken provider cannot lock you out.
sso.localLoginNeedsProvider: Add and activate a provider before turning off password sign-in.
sso.localLoginDisabled: Password sign-in disabled for everyone except system admins.

flaky.title: Flaky tests
flaky.hint: These cases keep changing outcome across recent runs.
flaky.explanation: The score counts how often consecutive runs disagreed, not how often the test failed. A test that always fails is broken, not flaky, and scores 0%.

version.title: Version history
version.hint: Every edit snapshots the previous wording, so you can see what a past run actually executed. Attachments are not versioned: adding or removing one shows in the project activity.
version.noHistory: This test case has not been edited yet, so there is nothing to compare.
version.label: v{{number}}

requirement.title: Requirements
requirement.cardHint: Trace requirements to tests and see coverage.
requirement.description: Link requirements to the test cases that prove them, and see what is actually covered.
requirement.externalIdHint: The id used in your spec or tracker.
requirement.name: Title
requirement.deleteMessage: {{id}} will be removed. The test cases linked to it are not affected.
requirement.noCases: No test cases linked — this requirement is unproven.
requirement.coverageNote: Requirements whose linked tests have passed

statusHint.PASSED: Every linked test passed in its most recent run.
statusHint.FAILED: At least one linked test failed most recently.
statusHint.BLOCKED: At least one linked test was blocked.
statusHint.UNTESTED: A test is linked but has never been executed, so nothing proves this requirement yet.
statusHint.UNCOVERED: No test case is linked to this requirement.

parameter.title: Parameters
parameter.hint: Give this case data sets and it runs once per set, with {placeholder} values substituted into the steps.
parameter.empty: No parameter sets — this case runs once, as normal.
parameter.setNameHint: Shown on each expanded result, e.g. "minimum" or "invalid email".
parameter.unresolved: No value for {{keys}} — the step will show the placeholder as written.
parameter.deleteMessage: {{name}} will be removed and future runs will no longer include it.
parameter.deleteKeepsResults: Results already recorded keep the values they ran with.

roles.projectAdmin: You administer at least one project, so the administration chapters are shown.
roles.tester: You can write test cases and carry out runs, so the authoring chapters are shown.
roles.viewer: You have read access, so this manual covers reading and following test results.
roles.none: You are not a member of any project yet. Ask an administrator to add you.

environment.label: Environment
environment.title: Environments
environment.description: Where tests run, e.g. Staging or Chrome · Production. Runs and bug reports pick from this list.
environment.empty: No environments yet. They are also added automatically when a run, bug report or CI upload names a new one.
environment.activeHint: Active environments are offered in pickers. Archived ones stay on past runs.
environment.inUseHint: In use. Archive it, or merge it into another environment.

merge.title: Merge "{{name}}"
merge.explanation: Moves its {{runs}} runs and {{bugs}} bug reports to the environment you pick, then deletes "{{name}}". This can't be undone.

review.title: Review
review.legacyApproved: Approved before review was switched on for this project.
review.bulkHint: Approved is set only by approving a case in review.

settings.title: Test case review
settings.description: Cases become Approved only after another member reviews them. Edits to the wording send an approved case back to review.
settings.tooFewReviewers: Fewer than two members can approve, so some cases may have nobody to review them.

session.title: Exploratory sessions
session.description: Time-boxed exploration against a charter. Log what you notice as you go, then debrief.
session.cardHint: Time-boxed exploration with a note log
session.debriefHint: What did you cover, what did you find, what's left?
session.notePlaceholder: What did you notice? Enter saves, Alt+1..4 picks the type, paste attaches a screenshot

form.title: New exploratory session
form.charterHint: e.g. Explore checkout with unusual currencies to discover rounding problems

customField.title: Custom fields
customField.description: Extra typed fields on this project's test cases, test runs and bug reports, such as Component, Sprint or Customer.
customField.full: At most {{max}} active fields; archive one first.
customField.activeHint: Active. Switch off to archive: the field is hidden from forms and filters, and its values are kept.

forceDelete.title: Delete field and its values?
forceDelete.message: "{{name}}" holds values. Deleting it discards them on every item, and this cannot be undone.
forceDelete.archiveInstead: To keep the values, cancel and archive the field instead.

dialog.name: Name
dialog.typeFixed: The type can't be changed. Create a new field and archive this one.
dialog.renameHint: Editing an option renames it everywhere it is used. An option that is in use can't be removed.
dialog.requiredHint: People must fill it in when saving a form. Imports, CI uploads and API agents are never blocked.

longDuration.title: Save a long duration?
longDuration.message: This records {{minutes}} minutes, more than 8 hours. If the timer ran while you were away, choose Cancel: the status is saved without a duration, and you can type the real time.

burnDown.title: Burn-down
burnDown.liveEstimates: Uses each test case's current estimate, so changing an estimate also moves past days.
burnDown.historyFrom: Results executed before execution times were recorded are not included; complete from {{date}}.
burnDown.noEstimates: None of this plan's test cases has an estimate yet, so there is nothing to burn down.

readiness.title: Release readiness
readiness.effectiveHint: Each test case's latest result across this plan's runs, so a failure retested and passed counts once, as a pass. Pending counts as not passed. The plan's pass rate above counts every result, so the two can differ. If a case ran in several environments, the latest run wins.
readiness.noCriteria: This plan has no release gate. Edit the plan to set thresholds.
readiness.counts: Latest results: {{passed}} passed, {{failed}} failed, {{blocked}} blocked, {{skipped}} skipped, {{pending}} pending, of {{considered}}.

gate.title: Release gate
gate.hint: Optional. The plan's readiness is GO when every threshold you set is met; leave a field empty to not use it. CI can check it through the API.

compare.title: Compare runs
compare.autoBase: Picked automatically: the previous run with the same name, or of the same plan and environment.
compare.baseNewer: The base ran after the head, so "newly failing" and "fixed" read backwards.
compare.noDifferences: No differences: every result is the same in both runs.
compare.versionChangedHint: The test case's wording changed between the two executions.
compare.duplicatesHint: A run recorded this case more than once; the worst result is shown.

sharedStep.title: Shared steps
sharedStep.cardHint: Blocks of steps kept once and used by many test cases
sharedStep.description: A shared step is a block of steps, such as "Log in as admin", kept once and used by any number of test cases. Edit it here and every test case using it follows, as do runs created afterwards.
sharedStep.emptyHint: No shared steps yet. Create one for steps you keep copying between test cases.
sharedStep.editWarning: Used by {{count}} test case(s). Saving changes the steps of all of them; each keeps a version with its previous wording, and in a project that requires review they go back to review.
sharedStep.notUsed: No test case uses this shared step.
sharedStep.deleteConfirm: Delete this shared step? This is only possible while no test case uses it.
sharedStep.emptyWarning: This shared step has no steps, so it adds nothing when run.
sharedStep.editedElsewhere: Its steps are edited on the shared step's own page.
sharedStep.convertConfirm: Replace this shared step with a copy of its steps? The test case stops following the shared step; later edits to it no longer reach this case.

attachment.title: Attachments
attachment.dropHint: or drop a file here. Images, PDF, ZIP, Office documents and text files up to 10 MB.
attachment.duplicate: An identical file is already attached as "{{name}}".
attachment.tooLarge: The file is larger than 10 MB.
attachment.uploadFailed: The file could not be uploaded.
